program_name: Computer Data Center Equipment Exemption Program
legal_authority: Act 84 of 2016, amended by Act 13 of 2019 and Act 25 of 2021; 72 P.S. § 9931-D
what_is_exempt: Computer data center equipment installed in a certified data center; excludes local sales tax, labor, maintenance contracts, and tools
job_requirement: 25 new jobs (county of 250,000 or fewer); 45 new jobs (larger county)
wage_requirement: At least $1M aggregate annual compensation at the site after the fourth anniversary of certification
benefit_duration: 25 full calendar years after the application year; qualified tenants up to 10 years
clawback_or_recapture: Department may revoke certification and recapture all or part of benefits if requirements are not met
energy_or_water_conditions: Since an Aug. 18, 2026 executive order, access to the exemption is conditioned on the governor's GRID standards, which include environmental, economic, and transparency requirements; PUC separately proposed a large-load tariff framework. In addition, the FY 2026-27 Fiscal Code (Act 21 of 2026) requires data centers of 10 MW or more to report energy and water use annually to DEP starting in 2027
public_reporting: Annual list of certifications; no reporting requirement at time of purchase, so actual cost is unknown. Not included in the IFO's annual incentive report, which covers tax credits, spending and grants, job training, and loans (Sept 2026). Under EO 2026-05, projects that sign a GRID Consent Order and Agreement must also report annual energy and water metrics to DEP and the Department of Revenue, tied to the exemption program guidelines
formal_evaluation: None; as a sales tax exemption it falls outside the Act 48 tax credit review cycle
status_2026: In effect. In June 2026 the House passed a repeal bill (HB 2198, 197-5) and the Senate passed repeal language in a separate tax code bill (HB 1667, 44-6), but neither reached the governor before the July 12 budget. An Aug. 18, 2026 executive order conditions the exemption on the governor's GRID standards. The Senate has not acted on the House-passed repeal (HB 2198) this fall

program_name: Data Center Retail Sales and Use Tax Exemption
administering_agency: Virginia Economic Development Partnership (MOU) and Department of Taxation
what_is_exempt: Computer equipment and enabling software, including servers, routers, chillers, and backup generators
job_requirement: 50 new jobs; 10 in distressed localities (unemployment and poverty above statewide rates)
wage_requirement: Jobs must pay at least 1.5 times the prevailing average wage in the locality
program_sunset: June 30, 2035; extensions to 2040 ($35B investment, 1,000 jobs) or 2050 ($100B investment)
clawback_or_recapture: MOU with VEDP sets repayment obligations if investment and job goals are not met
energy_or_water_conditions: None in the exemption; 2026 bills to add clean-energy conditions failed. EO 22 (Sept. 2026) adds environmental standards but does not tie them to the exemption
public_reporting: Operators report to VEDP; biennial report with return-on-investment analysis
evaluation_finding: Influential factor in data center growth; moderate economic benefits
status_2026: In effect; 2026-28 budget kept exemption, added a separate electricity tax, and ordered a tax policy study due Dec 15, 2026; a Sept. 18, 2026 executive order (EO 22) set new data center accountability standards but did not change the exemption or require companies to meet the standards to receive it

program_name: Data Center Sales and Use Tax Exemption
what_is_exempt: Computer data center equipment, including delivery, installation, and repair; construction materials
job_requirement: No job count in statute; payroll requirement applies instead
benefit_duration: Set in each agreement (examples: 10 and 15 years); exemption may be full or partial
clawback_or_recapture: Authority may reduce the exemption's percentage or term for noncompliance; if operations cease, it may terminate the agreement and require repayment of all or part of previously exempted taxes
public_reporting: Companies report annually to the Development director (financial details confidential); director reports annually by Aug 1 to the governor and legislative leaders on agreements and project status
formal_evaluation: None identified; statute requires an annual status report, not an effectiveness evaluation
estimated_annual_cost: State only, calendar years: $554.9M (2024); about $1.57B (2025), against a $136M forecast for 2025. Local sales tax losses: $166.8M (2024); $446.3M (2025)
status_2026: New applications paused since May 27, 2026, through the end of Gov. DeWine's term; existing agreements continue; the legislature did not agree on reform in June; repeal bills (HB 975, SB 374) in committee

program_name: Data Center Maryland Sales and Use Tax Exemption
administering_agency: Department of Commerce (certification) and Comptroller (exemption certificate)
what_is_exempt: Qualified data center personal property; electricity is not exempt
wage_requirement: Full-time, net new, at least 150% of state minimum wage
benefit_duration: 10 years, renewed annually; 20 years with $250M+ investment
clawback_or_recapture: Annual renewal; failure to maintain thresholds jeopardizes the exemption
public_reporting: Annual reports to Commerce; neither Commerce nor the Comptroller has data on the value of exemptions used
estimated_annual_cost: No official figure (10 approved data centers as of Feb 2026)
status_2026: In effect; Sept 23, 2026 executive order put Gov. Moore on record for repeal; repeal bill HB 560 saw no action after hearing

what_is_exempt: High-technology data center equipment and certain construction materials; state and local sales tax
minimum_investment: $250M (county population over 50,000); $75M (30,001 to 50,000); $25M (30,000 or fewer); over a seven-year investment period
job_requirement: 25 new quality jobs (county over 50,000); 10 (30,001 to 50,000); 5 (30,000 or fewer)
wage_requirement: Quality jobs must pay at least 110% of county average wage
clawback_or_recapture: Revenue commissioner may require a bond of up to $20M, forfeited if the minimum investment is not met
public_reporting: Final report to Department of Revenue after seven-year investment period
formal_evaluation: Yes: Department of Audits and Accounts (2022; updated 2025)
evaluation_finding: Negative net fiscal impact; about 70% of activity would have occurred without the exemption
estimated_annual_cost: State and local: about $2.5B projected for FY 2026 (Governor's tax expenditure report), against a $327M earlier estimate. State only: $474M in FY 2025 (University of Georgia audit)
status_2026: In effect; 2026 bills to repeal, suspend, or sunset early did not pass
items_to_verify: Whether repayment of exempted taxes applies beyond the bond
